summary:
WallkiHealth means “Health Companion.” Its name is inspired by *Wallki*, a word associated with companionship in the Ancash variety of Central Quechua, an Indigenous language of Peru.

WallkiHealth is an educational, AI-assisted platform designed to support astronaut health during long-duration space missions. It integrates daily vital-sign monitoring, health records, personalized preventive guidance, medical follow-up, and early alerts into one accessible system.

By monitoring heart rate, oxygen levels, blood pressure, sleep, stress, and radiation exposure, WallkiHealth helps astronauts and medical teams identify potential health changes and make informed decisions.

Developed independently in Peru, WallkiHealth combines artificial intelligence, technology, and Andean cultural inspiration with one purpose: to be a trusted health companion for astronauts beyond Earth.
details:
WALLKIHEALTH: HEALTH SUPPORT FOR SPACE MISSIONS

WallkiHealth is a web platform designed to support astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions. It lets users record and review daily vital signs and health habits, including heart rate, blood oxygen, temperature, blood pressure, sleep, exercise, stress, and radiation exposure. It brings health history, preventive alerts, personalized guidance, and medical follow-up notes together in one application.

The platform organizes information so crew members can review their own records and authorized administrators or medical staff can monitor trends and identify changes that may need follow-up. It includes crew profiles, role-based accounts, historical charts, data export, and an optional AI-assisted guidance feature. WallkiHealth is a prototype; its alerts are informational and it does not diagnose or replace evaluation by a healthcare professional.

WallkiHealth aims to make health records easier to maintain and review during isolated missions. By bringing physiological measurements together with spaceflight factors such as radiation exposure, isolation, and sleep, it can help astronauts and medical teams discuss changes in well-being and decide when closer attention may be appropriate. The project demonstrates a practical way to organize this information; it is not a clinically or spaceflight-validated medical device.

WallkiHealth was built with React and Vite for the web interface, Python and Flask for the API, and SQLite for data storage. It supports local authentication and Google sign-in, trend visualization, record export, and English and Spanish. The guidance assistant can optionally connect to Gemini; when it is not configured, the application provides local preventive guidance.

The project brings health monitoring, spaceflight risk factors, and communication tools into a straightforward experience for crew members and medical staff. The name WallkiHealth means “Health Companion” and is inspired by “Wallki,” a word associated with companionship in the Ancash variety of Central Quechua. This Andean cultural inspiration connects the idea of companionship with the challenge of supporting human health beyond Earth.

WallkiHealth was developed independently in Peru by IVAN TEODOLIO MOYA HUAYTAN.
